title: Discrete continuous modules embed in coinduced modules
statement: Let $G$ be a profinite group, $A$ a finite ring, and $M$ a left $A$-module with an action of $G$ by $A$-linear automorphisms such that each $m\in M$ has open stabilizer [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian]. Give $M$ the discrete topology and put $D(M)=\operatorname{Cont}(G,M)$, with pointwise $A$-module structure and left $G$-action $(h\cdot f)(x)=f(xh)$. Every $f\in D(M)$ has open stabilizer, so $D(M)$ is again an object of the same category. The map $\iota_M:M\to D(M)$ defined by $\iota_M(m)(x)=x m$ is $A$-linear, $G$-equivariant, injective, and natural in $M$.

proof.text: Pointwise addition and scalar multiplication make $D(M)=\operatorname{Cont}(G,M)$ an $A$-module. For $h,k\in G$ and $f\in D(M)$, $((hk)\cdot f)(x)=f(xhk)=(h\cdot(k\cdot f))(x)$ and $(1\cdot f)(x)=f(x)$, so $(h\cdot f)(x)=f(xh)$ is a left action. Each translate is $A$-linear and continuous because it is precomposition by the homeomorphism $x\mapsto xh$.

source.place: Tag 04JP, label definition-G-module-continuous; the action calculation is the agent-written construction used with Tag 0DVG

proof.text: For $f\in D(M)$, apply [lem-exc-coinduced-functions-open-stabilizer] to obtain an open normal subgroup $U$ with $f(xu)=f(x)$ for all $x\in G$ and $u\in U$. Thus $(u\cdot f)(x)=f(xu)=f(x)$, so $U$ is contained in the stabilizer of $f$. A subgroup containing an open subgroup is open, hence every element of $D(M)$ has open stabilizer and $D(M)$ is an object of the same category of discrete continuous $G$-modules.

Define $\iota_M(m)(x)=xm$. This function is continuous: the stabilizer of $m$ is open, and the orbit map is constant on each left coset $xH$ of the stabilizer $H$ of $m$, since $x h m=x m$ for $h\in H$. It is $A$-linear pointwise. For $h,x\in G$, $(h\cdot\iota_M(m))(x)=\iota_M(m)(xh)=(xh)m=x(hm)=\iota_M(hm)(x)$, so it is $G$-equivariant. Evaluation at the identity gives $\iota_M(m)(1)=m$, proving injectivity. If $u:M\to N$ is an equivariant $A$-linear map, then $(D(u)\circ\iota_M)(m)(x)=u(xm)=x u(m)=(\iota_N\circ u)(m)(x)$, so the construction is natural in $M$.
